NASB.1: 'Coastlands, listen to Me in silence, And let the peoples gain new strength; Let them come forward, then let them speak; Let us come together for judgment.
NASB.2: 'Who has aroused one from the east Whom He calls in righteousness to His feet? He delivers up nations before him And subdues kings. He makes them like dust with his sword, As the wind-driven chaff with his bow.
NASB.3: 'He pursues them, passing on in safety, By a way he had not been traversing with his feet.
NASB.4: 'Who has performed and accomplished [it], Calling forth the generations from the beginning? 'I, the LORD, am the first, and with the last. I am He.''
NASB.5: The coastlands have seen and are afraid; The ends of the earth tremble; They have drawn near and have come.
NASB.6: Each one helps his neighbor And says to his brother, 'Be strong!'
NASB.7: So the craftsman encourages the smelter, [And] he who smooths [metal] with the hammer [encourages] him who beats the anvil, Saying of the soldering, 'It is good'; And he fastens it with nails, [So that] it will not totter.
NASB.8: 'But you, Israel, My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, Descendant of Abraham My friend,
NASB.9: You whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, And called from its remotest parts And said to you, 'You are My servant, I have chosen you and not rejected you.
NASB.10: 'Do not fear, for I am with you; Do not anxiously look about you, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, surely I will help you, Surely I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.'
NASB.11: 'Behold, all those who are angered at you will be shamed and dishonored; Those who contend with you will be as nothing and will perish.
NASB.12: 'You will seek those who quarrel with you, but will not find them, Those who war with you will be as nothing and non-existent.
NASB.13: 'For I am the LORD your God, who upholds your right hand, Who says to you, 'Do not fear, I will help you.'
NASB.14: 'Do not fear, you worm Jacob, you men of Israel; I will help you,' declares the LORD, 'and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
NASB.15: 'Behold, I have made you a new, sharp threshing sledge with double edges; You will thresh the mountains and pulverize [them], And will make the hills like chaff.
NASB.16: 'You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, And the storm will scatter them; But you will rejoice in the LORD, You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
NASB.17: 'The afflicted and needy are seeking water, but there is none, And their tongue is parched with thirst; I, the LORD, will answer them Myself, [As] the God of Israel I will not forsake them.
NASB.18: 'I will open rivers on the bare heights And springs in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water And the dry land fountains of water.
NASB.19: 'I will put the cedar in the wilderness, The acacia and the myrtle and the olive tree; I will place the juniper in the desert Together with the box tree and the cypress,
NASB.20: That they may see and recognize, And consider and gain insight as well, That the hand of the LORD has done this, And the Holy One of Israel has created it.
NASB.21: 'Present your case,' the LORD says. 'Bring forward your strong [arguments],' The King of Jacob says.
NASB.22: Let them bring forth and declare to us what is going to take place; As for the former [events], declare what they [were], That we may consider them and know their outcome. Or announce to us what is coming;
NASB.23: Declare the things that are going to come afterward, That we may know that you are gods; Indeed, do good or evil, that we may anxiously look about us and fear together.
NASB.24: Behold, you are of no account, And your work amounts to nothing; He who chooses you is an abomination.
NASB.25: 'I have aroused one from the north, and he has come; From the rising of the sun he will call on My name; And he will come upon rulers as [upon] mortar, Even as the potter treads clay.'
NASB.26: Who has declared [this] from the beginning, that we might know? Or from former times, that we may say, '[He is] right!'? Surely there was no one who declared, Surely there was no one who proclaimed, Surely there was no one who heard your words.
NASB.27: 'Formerly [I said] to Zion, 'Behold, here they are.' And to Jerusalem, 'I will give a messenger of good news.'
NASB.28: 'But when I look, there is no one, And there is no counselor among them Who, if I ask, can give an answer.
NASB.29: 'Behold, all of them are false; Their works are worthless, Their molten images are wind and emptiness.

ESV.1: Listen to me in silence, O coastlands; let the peoples renew their strength; let them approach, then let them speak; let us together draw near for judgment.
ESV.2: Who stirred up one from the east whom victory meets at every step?  He gives up nations before him, so that he tramples kings underfoot; he makes them like dust with his sword, like driven stubble with his bow.
ESV.3: He pursues them and passes on safely, by paths his feet have not trod.
ESV.4: Who has performed and done this, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, the first, and with the last; I am he.
ESV.5: The coastlands have seen and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble; they have drawn near and come.
ESV.6: Everyone helps his neighbor and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
ESV.7: The craftsman strengthens the goldsmith, and he who smooths with the hammer him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good”; and they strengthen it with nails so that it cannot be moved.
ESV.8: But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, my friend;
ESV.9: you whom I took from the ends of the earth, and called from its farthest corners, saying to you, “You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you off”;
ESV.10: fear not, for I am with you; be not dismayed, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
ESV.11: Behold, all who are incensed against you shall be put to shame and confounded; those who strive against you shall be as nothing and shall perish.
ESV.12: You shall seek those who contend with you, but you shall not find them; those who war against you shall be as nothing at all.
ESV.13: For I, the LORD your God, hold your right hand; it is I who say to you, “Fear not, I am the one who helps you.”
ESV.14: Fear not, you worm Jacob, you men of Israel! I am the one who helps you, declares the LORD; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
ESV.15: Behold, I make of you a threshing sledge, new, sharp, and having teeth; you shall thresh the mountains and crush them, and you shall make the hills like chaff;
ESV.16: you shall winnow them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the tempest shall scatter them. And you shall rejoice in the LORD; in the Holy One of Israel you shall glory.
ESV.17: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue is parched with thirst, I the LORD will answer them; I the God of Israel will not forsake them.
ESV.18: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
ESV.19: I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the olive. I will set in the desert the cypress, the plane and the pine together,
ESV.20: that they may see and know, may consider and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, the Holy One of Israel has created it.
ESV.21: Set forth your case, says the LORD; bring your proofs, says the King of Jacob.
ESV.22: Let them bring them, and tell us what is to happen. Tell us the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, that we may know their outcome; or declare to us the things to come.
ESV.23: Tell us what is to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods; do good, or do harm, that we may be dismayed and terrified.
ESV.24: Behold, you are nothing, and your work is less than nothing; an abomination is he who chooses you.
ESV.25: I stirred up one from the north, and he has come, from the rising of the sun, and he shall call upon my name; he shall trample on rulers as on mortar, as the potter treads clay.
ESV.26: Who declared it from the beginning, that we might know, and beforehand, that we might say, “He is right”? There was none who declared it, none who proclaimed, none who heard your words.
ESV.27: I was the first to say  to Zion, “Behold, here they are!” and I give to Jerusalem a herald of good news.
ESV.28: But when I look, there is no one; among these there is no counselor who, when I ask, gives an answer.
ESV.29: Behold, they are all a delusion; their works are nothing; their metal images are empty wind.

NKJV.1: “Keep silence before Me, O coastlands, And let the people renew their strength! Let them come near, then let them speak; Let us come near together for judgment.
NKJV.2: “Who raised up one from the east? Who in righteousness called him to His feet? Who gave the nations before him, And made him rule over kings? Who gave them as the dust to his sword, As driven stubble to his bow?
NKJV.3: Who pursued them, and passed safely By the way that he had not gone with his feet?
NKJV.4: Who has performed and done it, Calling the generations from the beginning? ‘I, the LORD, am the first; And with the last I am He.’ ”
NKJV.5: The coastlands saw it and feared, The ends of the earth were afraid; They drew near and came.
NKJV.6: Everyone helped his neighbor, And said to his brother, “Be of good courage!”
NKJV.7: So the craftsman encouraged the goldsmith; He who smooths with the hammer inspired him who strikes the anvil, Saying, “It is ready for the soldering”; Then he fastened it with pegs, That it might not totter.
NKJV.8: “But you, Israel, are My servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, The descendants of Abraham My friend.
NKJV.9: You whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, And called from its farthest regions, And said to you, ‘You are My servant, I have chosen you and have not cast you away:
NKJV.10: Fear not, for I am with you; Be not dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you, Yes, I will help you, I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.’
NKJV.11: “Behold, all those who were incensed against you Shall be ashamed and disgraced; They shall be as nothing, And those who strive with you shall perish.
NKJV.12: You shall seek them and not find them— Those who contended with you. Those who war against you Shall be as nothing, As a nonexistent thing.
NKJV.13: For I, the LORD your God, will hold your right hand, Saying to you, ‘Fear not, I will help you.’
NKJV.14: “Fear not, you worm Jacob, You men of Israel! I will help you,” says the LORD And your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
NKJV.15: “Behold, I will make you into a new threshing sledge with sharp teeth; You shall thresh the mountains and beat them small, And make the hills like chaff.
NKJV.16: You shall winnow them, the wind shall carry them away, And the whirlwind shall scatter them; You shall rejoice in the LORD, And glory in the Holy One of Israel.
NKJV.17: “The poor and needy seek water, but there is none, Their tongues fail for thirst. I, the LORD, will hear them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
NKJV.18: I will open rivers in desolate heights, And fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, And the dry land springs of water.
NKJV.19: I will plant in the wilderness the cedar and the acacia tree, The myrtle and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the cypress tree and the pine And the box tree together,
NKJV.20: That they may see and know, And consider and understand together, That the hand of the LORD has done this, And the Holy One of Israel has created it.
NKJV.21: “Present your case,” says the LORD. “Bring forth your strong reasons,” says the King of Jacob.
NKJV.22: “Let them bring forth and show us what will happen; Let them show the former things, what they were, That we may consider them, And know the latter end of them; Or declare to us things to come.
NKJV.23: Show the things that are to come hereafter, That we may know that you are gods; Yes, do good or do evil, That we may be dismayed and see it together.
NKJV.24: Indeed you are nothing, And your work is nothing; He who chooses you is an abomination.
NKJV.25: “I have raised up one from the north, And he shall come; From the rising of the sun he shall call on My name; And he shall come against princes as though mortar, As the potter treads clay.
NKJV.26: Who has declared from the beginning, that we may know? And former times, that we may say, ‘He is righteous’? Surely there is no one who shows, Surely there is no one who declares, Surely there is no one who hears your words.
NKJV.27: The first time I said to Zion, ‘Look, there they are!’ And I will give to Jerusalem one who brings good tidings.
NKJV.28: For I looked, and there was no man; I looked among them, but there was no counselor, Who, when I asked of them, could answer a word.
NKJV.29: Indeed they are all worthless; Their works are nothing; Their molded images are wind and confusion.

AMP.1:
"Listen to Me in silence, you islands and coastlands,
And let the nations gain their strength;
Let them come near, then let them speak;
Let us come together for judgment [and decide the issue between us concerning the enemy from the east].
AMP.2:
"Who has stirred up and put into action one from the east [the king of Persia, Cyrus the Great]
Whom He calls in righteousness to His service and whom victory meets at every step?
The LORD turns nations over to him
And subdues kings.
He makes them like dust with his sword,
Like wind-driven chaff with his bow.
AMP.3:
"He (Cyrus) pursues them and passes along safely,
By a way his feet had not traveled before.
AMP.4:
"Who has performed and done this,
Calling forth [and guiding the destinies of] the generations [of the nations] from the beginning?
'I, the LORD—the first, and with the last [existing before history began, the ever-present, unchanging God]—I am He.'"
AMP.5:
The islands and coastlands have seen and they fear;
The ends of the earth tremble;
They have drawn near and have come.
AMP.6:
They each help his neighbor
And say to his brother [as he fashions his idols], "Be of good courage!"
AMP.7:
So the craftsman encourages the goldsmith,
And he who smooths metal with the smith's hammer encourages him who beats the anvil,
Saying of the soldering (welding), "That is good";
And he fastens the idol with nails,
So that it will not totter nor be moved.
AMP.8:
"But you, Israel, My servant,
Jacob whom I have chosen,
The offspring of Abraham My friend,
AMP.9:
You whom I [the LORD] have taken from the ends of the earth,
And called from its remotest parts
And said to you, 'You are My servant,
I have chosen you and have not rejected you [even though you are exiled].
AMP.10:
'Do not fear [anything], for I am with you;
Do not be afraid, for I am your God.
I will strengthen you, be assured I will help you;
I will certainly take hold of you with My righteous right hand [a hand of justice, of power, of victory, of salvation].'
AMP.11:
"Indeed, all those who are angry with you will be put to shame and humiliated;
Those who strive against you will be as nothing and will perish.
AMP.12:
"You shall search for those who quarrel with you, but will not find them;
They who war against you will be as nothing, as nothing at all.
AMP.13:
"For I the LORD your God keep hold of your right hand; [I am the Lord],
Who says to you, 'Do not fear, I will help you.'
AMP.14:
"Do not fear, you worm Jacob, you men of Israel;
I will help you," declares the LORD, "and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
AMP.15:
"In fact, I have made of you a new, sharp threshing implement with sharp edges;
You will thresh the mountains and crush them,
And make the hills like chaff.
AMP.16:
"You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away,
And a high wind will scatter them;
But you will rejoice in the LORD,
You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
AMP.17:
"The poor and needy are seeking water, but there is none;
Their tongues are parched with thirst.
I, the LORD, will answer them Myself;
I, the God of Israel, will not neglect them.
AMP.18:
"I will open rivers on the barren heights
And springs in the midst of the valleys;
I will make the wilderness a reed-pool of water

NLT.1:

Remote lands tremble and mobilize for war.
NLT.6:
The idol makers encourage one another,
saying to each other, “Be strong!”

Jacob my chosen one,
descended from Abraham my friend,

I have called you back from the ends of the earth,

and will not throw you away.
NLT.10:
Don’t be afraid, for I am with you.

I will strengthen you and help you.

NLT.11:
“See, all your angry enemies lie there,

and come to nothing.

You will look in vain

will come to nothing.

‘Don’t be afraid. I am here to help you.

NLT.15:
You will be a new threshing instrument
with many sharp teeth.

making chaff of mountains.
NLT.16:

You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.

I pulled you in from all over the world,
called you in from every dark corner of the earth,
Telling you, 'You're my servant, serving on my side.
I've picked you. I haven't dropped you.'
MSG.10:
Don't panic. I'm with you.
There's no need to fear for I'm your God.
I'll give you strength. I'll help you.
I'll hold you steady, keep a firm grip on you.
MSG.11:
"Count on it: Everyone who had it in for you
will end up out in the cold—
real losers.
Those who worked against you
will end up empty-handed—
nothing to show for their lives.
MSG.12:
When you go out looking for your old adversaries
you won't find them—
Not a trace of your old enemies,
not even a memory.
MSG.13:
That's right. Because I, your God,
have a firm grip on you and I'm not letting go.
I'm telling you, 'Don't panic.
I'm right here to help you.'
MSG.14:
"Do you feel like a lowly worm, Jacob?
Don't be afraid.
Feel like a fragile insect, Israel?
I'll help you.
I, God, want to reassure you.
The God who buys you back, The Holy of Israel.
MSG.15:
I'm transforming you from worm to harrow,
from insect to iron.
As a sharp-toothed harrow you'll smooth out the mountains,
turn those tough old hills into loamy soil.
MSG.16:
You'll open the rough ground to the weather,
to the blasts of sun and wind and rain.
But you'll be confident and exuberant,
expansive in The Holy of Israel!
MSG.17:
"The poor and homeless are desperate for water,
their tongues parched and no water to be found.
But I'm there to be found, I'm there for them,
and I, God of Israel, will not leave them thirsty.
MSG.18:
I'll open up rivers for them on the barren hills,
spout fountains in the valleys.
I'll turn the baked-clay badlands into a cool pond,
the waterless waste into splashing creeks.
MSG.19:
I'll plant the red cedar in that treeless wasteland,
also acacia, myrtle, and olive.
I'll place the cypress in the desert,
with plenty of oaks and pines.
MSG.20:
Everyone will see this. No one can miss it—
unavoidable, indisputable evidence
That I, God, personally did this.
It's created and signed by The Holy of Israel.
MSG.21:
"Set out your case for your gods," says God.
"Bring your evidence," says the King of Jacob.
MSG.22:
"Take the stand on behalf of your idols, offer arguments,
assemble reasons.
Spread out the facts before us
so that we can assess them ourselves.
Ask them, 'If you are gods, explain what the past means—
MSG.23:
or, failing that, tell us what will happen in the future.
Can't do that?
How about doing something—anything!
Good or bad—whatever.
Can you hurt us or help us? Do we need to be afraid?'
MSG.24:
They say nothing, because they are nothing—
sham gods, no-gods, fool-making gods.
MSG.25:
"I, God, started someone out from the north and he's come.
He was called out of the east by name.
He'll stomp the rulers into the mud
the way a potter works the clay.
MSG.26:
Let me ask you, Did anyone guess that this might happen?
Did anyone tell us earlier so we might confirm it
with 'Yes, he's right!'?
No one mentioned it, no one announced it,
no one heard a peep out of you.
MSG.27:
But I told Zion all about this beforehand.
I gave Jerusalem a preacher of good news.
MSG.28:
But around here there's no one—
no one who knows what's going on.
I ask, but no one can tell me the score.
MSG.29:
Nothing here. It's all smoke and hot air—
sham gods, hollow gods, no-gods.

NET.1: “Listen to me in silence, you coastlands! Let the nations find renewed strength! Let them approach and then speak; let us come together for debate!
NET.2: Who stirs up this one from the east? Who officially commissions him for service? He hands nations over to him, and enables him to subdue kings. He makes them like dust with his sword, like windblown straw with his bow.
NET.3: He pursues them and passes by unharmed; he advances with great speed.
NET.4: Who acts and carries out decrees? Who summons the successive generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, am present at the very beginning, and at the very end — I am the one.
NET.5: The coastlands see and are afraid; the whole earth trembles; they approach and come.
NET.6: They help one another; one says to the other, ‘Be strong!’
NET.7: The craftsman encourages the metalsmith, the one who wields the hammer encourages the one who pounds on the anvil. He approves the quality of the welding, and nails it down so it won’t fall over.”
NET.8: “You, my servant Israel, Jacob whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my friend,
NET.9: you whom I am bringing back from the earth’s extremities, and have summoned from the remote regions — I told you, “You are my servant.” I have chosen you and not rejected you.
NET.10: Don’t be afraid, for I am with you! Don’t be frightened, for I am your God! I strengthen you — yes, I help you — yes, I uphold you with my saving right hand!
NET.11: Look, all who were angry at you will be ashamed and humiliated; your adversaries will be reduced to nothing and perish.
NET.12: When you will look for your opponents, you will not find them; your enemies will be reduced to absolutely nothing.
NET.13: For I am the LORD your God, the one who takes hold of your right hand, who says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, I am helping you.’
NET.14: Don’t be afraid, despised insignificant Jacob, men of Israel. I am helping you,” says the LORD, your protector, the Holy One of Israel.
NET.15: “Look, I am making you like a sharp threshing sledge, new and double-edged. You will thresh the mountains and crush them; you will make the hills like straw.
NET.16: You will winnow them and the wind will blow them away; the wind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD; you will boast in the Holy One of Israel.
NET.17: The oppressed and the poor look for water, but there is none; their tongues are parched from thirst. I, the LORD, will respond to their prayers; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
NET.18: I will make streams flow down the slopes and produce springs in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the desert into a pool of water and the arid land into springs.
NET.19: I will make cedars, acacias, myrtles, and olive trees grow in the wilderness; I will make evergreens, firs, and cypresses grow together in the desert.
NET.20: I will do this so people will observe and recognize, so they will pay attention and understand that the LORD’s power has accomplished this, and that the Holy One of Israel has brought it into being.”
NET.21: “Present your argument,” says the LORD. “Produce your evidence,” says Jacob’s king.
NET.22: “Let them produce evidence! Let them tell us what will happen! Tell us about your earlier predictive oracles, so we may examine them and see how they were fulfilled. Or decree for us some future events!
NET.23: Predict how future events will turn out, so we might know you are gods. Yes, do something good or bad, so we might be frightened and in awe.
NET.24: Look, you are nothing, and your accomplishments are nonexistent; the one who chooses to worship you is disgusting.
NET.25: I have stirred up one out of the north and he advances, one from the eastern horizon who prays in my name. He steps on rulers as if they were clay, like a potter treading the clay.
NET.26: Who decreed this from the beginning, so we could know? Who announced it ahead of time, so we could say, ‘He’s correct’? Indeed, none of them decreed it! Indeed, none of them announced it! Indeed, no one heard you say anything!
NET.27: I first decreed to Zion, ‘Look, here’s what will happen!’ I sent a herald to Jerusalem.
NET.28: I look, but there is no one, among them there is no one who serves as an adviser, that I might ask questions and receive answers.
NET.29: Look, all of them are nothing, their accomplishments are nonexistent; their metal images lack any real substance.
